code: pp_vis <- pattern_profiler_analysis(   se_proc = res$se_proc,   DEPs_results = res$DEPs_results,   assay_name = "Impseqrob_min",   filter_mode = "any",   alpha = 0.05,   condition_order = c("A", "B", "D"),   aggregate = "median",   auto_select_c = FALSE,   c = 2,   min_membership = 0.25,   seed = 42,   verbose = FALSE ) display_membership <- 0.70 pp_display <- pp_vis$long_output[   pp_vis$long_output$Membership >= display_membership,   ,   drop = FALSE ]  pattern_summary <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(split(pp_display, pp_display$Cluster), function(x) {     data.frame(       Cluster = paste("Cluster", unique(x$Cluster)),       Proteins = length(unique(x$FeatureID)),       `Median membership` = median(x$Membership),       A = median(x$A),       B = median(x$B),       D = median(x$D),       check.names = FALSE     )   }) )  pattern_summary[c("Median membership", "A", "B", "D")] <- lapply(   pattern_summary[c("Median membership", "A", "B", "D")],   round,   digits = 3 )  knitr::kable(   pattern_summary,   row.names = FALSE,   caption = paste0(     "High-membership proteins and median z-score profiles at membership >= ",     display_membership, "."   ) )

text: SummarizedExperiment new corrected assay added. BERT returns fewer features input, SE subsetted match warning issued.

title: Batch Correction with BERT — batch_correct_proteomics
code: data(nadia_dia)  # nadia_dia has no batch information, so the example builds a plausible one: # two digestion batches crossed with the three conditions. cov <- data.frame(Column = nadia_dia$metadata$Coding,                   Batch = rep(c("b1", "b2"),                               length.out = nrow(nadia_dia$metadata)),                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE) res <- process_proteomics(nadia_dia, covariate_df = cov, verbose = FALSE)  # BERT removes the batch effect and adds a "BERT" assay, leaving the # original one untouched se <- batch_correct_proteomics(res$se_proc, assay_name = "Impseqrob_min",                                batch_column = "Batch", verbose = FALSE) #> Warning: batch_correct_proteomics: 'covariates = NULL' with algorithm='ComBat'. ComBat/limma remove ALL batch-associated variance; if the biological condition is (partially) confounded with the batch, real biological signal will be lost. Passing the condition variable in 'covariates' (batch_covariates) is recommended in order to preserve it. SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se) #> [1] "raw"           "log2"          "cycloess"      "Impseqrob_min" #> [5] "BERT"           # On a real experiment you would normally pass the biological variable of # interest in `covariates`, so that ComBat preserves it instead of removing # it along with the batch effect. `covariates = "Condition"` works on this # example: the assay is already imputed, so each batch-by-condition cell has # its two values. Before imputation, with only two samples per cell, BERT # needs two non-missing values per cell and any protein with a gap there # stops being adjustable.

Name assay use starting point (typically normalized assay, pre-imputation, real NAs). methods Character vector individual imputation methods benchmark. Default: .IM_BENCH_METHODS (16 methods). Use character(0) NULL skip individual methods. combo_methods Named list combo/softHybrid configurations. element list : mode ("combo" "softHybrid", default "combo"), mar_method, mnar_method. list name used method label results. Default: empty list (combo methods). condition_col Character. Column colData condition labels, required combo methods. Default "Condition". na_prop Numeric (0-1). Proportion artificial NAs. Default 0.20. used pattern = "random". Ignored pattern = "from_data" (NA proportion derived data, replicating NAguideR). seed Integer. Random seed. Default 42. pattern Character. NA introduction pattern: "random" uniform random NAs, "from_data" replicate NAguideR's simulation strategy (row ratio + per-column distribution actual data). method_args Named list per-method argument lists. with_value Constant value method "". verbose Logical. Print progress. Default TRUE.

title: Compute quantitative group-separation metrics per normalization method — nm_compute_metrics
text: data.frame one row per method columns: Method, PC1_VarPct, PC1_F_ratio, PERMANOVA_R2, PERMANOVA_pval, Silhouette_mean, MDS_GOF, MDS_CophCor, Spectral_Entropy, CumVar_PC2, Hopkins, Condition_Number.

title: Compute quantitative group-separation metrics per normalization method — nm_compute_metrics
text: PC1_VarPct: % variance explained PC1 (higher = structure). PC1_F_ratio: ANOVA F-ratio PC1 scores (higher = better separation). PERMANOVA_R2: Proportion variance explained grouping (requires vegan; NA installed). Silhouette_mean: Mean silhouette width (requires cluster; NA installed). MDS_GOF: Goodness--fit 2D MDS projection. Note: benchmarking context, lower values tend indicate better normalization (good method preserves multi-dimensional biological variability 2D capture). MDS_CophCor: Cophenetic correlation original MDS distances. caveat MDS_GOF: lower values tend correlate better benchmarking performance. Spectral_Entropy: Normalized Shannon entropy PCA eigenvalues (0-1). Values near 0 = variance concentrated PCs; near 1 = uniform spread. CumVar_PC2: Cumulative % variance explained PC1 + PC2 (0-100). Hopkins: Hopkins statistic clustering tendency (0-1). Values > 0.5 suggest non-random cluster structure. Condition_Number: Ratio largest smallest PCA eigenvalue (>= 1). High values indicate multicollinearity numerical instability.

title: Compute quantitative group-separation metrics per normalization method — nm_compute_metrics
code: data(nadia_dia) se <- nm_prepare_se(nadia_dia, verbose = FALSE) se <- nm_run_normalizations(se, methods = c("cycloess", "quantile", "MAD"),                             verbose = FALSE)  metrics_df <- nm_compute_metrics(se) metrics_df[, c("Method", "PC1_VarPct", "PC1_F_ratio", "Silhouette_mean")] #>     Method PC1_VarPct PC1_F_ratio Silhouette_mean #> 1     log2   56.03859    120.9196       0.2118819 #> 2 cycloess   72.57836   9790.2845       0.3790455 #> 3 quantile   65.48778  10168.4649       0.3760405 #> 4      MAD   64.86712   9803.3024       0.3862026
